newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-GRANT FLOWER LEADS FIGHTBACK AFTER NAZIR SHINES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GRANT FLOWER LEADS FIGHTBACK AFTER NAZIR SHINES.

text.p: Opener Grant Flower led a Zimbabwe fightback with an unbeaten 98 after Pakistan fast bowler Shahid Nazir marked his test debut with three wickets and a run out on Thursday.
Flower, with Paul Strang proving an effective ally by making 37 not out, hauled the touring team from 142 for six to 240 for six at the close on the opening day of the first test.

Zimbabwe had been plunged into trouble essentially by Nazir after they won the toss and opted to bat on a grassless pitch at the Sheikupura Stadium, hosting its first test to become Pakistan's 11th test ground.
Nazir, 19, took a wicket with his fourth ball and two more in consecutive deliveries, ending his first day in test cricket with three for 35.
After Wasim Akram made the initial breakthrough by having Mark Dekker lbw for 14, Nazir dealt his first blow when he sent back Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell lbw for eight.
Flower and David Houghton repaired the early damage, lifting the touring side from 41 for two to 106 for two at lunch, only for four wickets to go for 64 in the second session.
Nazir ended the third wicket stand of 78 when he ran out Houghton for an attractive 42, which contained three fours and two sixes, both off Saqlain Mushtaq's off-spin.
The debutant paceman then returned to account for Andy Flower (11) and Craig Wishart (0), trapping lbw with successive balls, but was denied a hat-trick.
Saqlain dispatched Guy Whittall, caught close in by Shadab Kabir, but Pakistan were denied further success by Grant Flower and Strang in their unfinished seventh wicket stand of 98.
Flower, who compiled 201 against Pakistan at Harare in the 1994-95 series, slammed 11 fours and a six and has faced 264 balls.
Strang had two fours and a six in his 121-ball knock spanning 165 minutes.
Play was twice stopped briefly after spectators, angered at the exclusion of local paceman Aqib Javed, pelted fielders with stones.
